operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers: Station_ID, Name, Annual_entry_exit, Train_ID, Station_ID; must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
Table train_station has composite PK (Train_ID, Station_ID) and two FKs to train and station; both parents exist and are unique.
All columns declared NOT NULL=0 (nullable) yet original null_rate=0 everywhere; TS may emit NULLs and inserts will succeed.
Time column is TEXT storing 'HH:MM' (e.g. '17:15', '4:49', '06:30') — no leading zero on some, so String fuzzer, not Time.
Service column has distinct=1 ('Daily') — String fuzzer will produce many distinct values, breaking any 'all Daily' assumption.
Location distinct=3 (London/Birmingham/Glasgow) — String fuzzer will not preserve this small enum.
Main_Services has trailing spaces in samples ('... West of England ') — string contamination/prefix-drop will mangle.
REAL columns (Annual_entry_exit, Annual_interchanges, Total_Passengers) hold values like 94.046 — Number fuzzer with scale from type args (none) => scale 0, so ints, contradicting real storage.
INT columns (Station_ID, Train_ID, Number_of_Platforms) are small ints 1..19; Number fuzzer range [-1,1] with scale 0 => mostly -1/0/1, poor coverage.
Tiny tables (12, 11, 11 rows) — choose_table_sizes will produce 1..~2500 rows, far larger than original; joins still work.
train_station.Station_ID distinct=7 < station rows=12 — FK child does not cover all parents; TS draws with replacement from parent values so coverage varies.
No views, triggers, indexes beyond PKs; DDL is simple, no CHECK/UNIQUE constraints to trip inserts.
operator_ts_expectations: Station_ID/Train_ID/Number_of_Platforms: Number fuzzer, scale 0 (no args), range [-1,1], int perturbation +-1/+-2 => values in {-3..3} mostly; PK uniqueness filter keeps few rows.
Annual_* / Total_Passengers: Number fuzzer scale 0 => integers, not reals; storage class becomes integer, contradicting declared REAL.
Name/Location/Main_Services/Service: String fuzzer, length range from samples (e.g. 0..~40), CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9() plus contamination => implausible station names, likely FN on name-matching queries.
Time: String fuzzer (declared TEXT) => random strings, not HH:MM; queries filtering on time format will miss (FN) or match spuriously (FP).
Service: String fuzzer ignores distinct=1 => many values, so 'Service = Daily' queries return few/no rows (FN).
Location: String fuzzer ignores 3-value enum => 'Location = London' returns few rows (FN).
train_station FK columns drawn from parent final values with replacement; composite PK dedup keeps first occurrence => small train_station, possibly empty if parents tiny.
Number fuzzer list_max quirk (overwrites with full-range max) means even with literal pool values, fresh draws dominate when p<rng.
p=0.2 default, 0.3 chance whole instance p=0 => 30% of instances are pure-literal (no fresh), 70% mix; checked columns none here so p not forced 0.
Date/Time fuzzers not dispatched (no date/timestamp/time declared types) — no date formatting issues.

Known misses: FN from implausible strings (names, services, locations) and wrong-format Time; FP from Number fuzzer producing small ints that accidentally satisfy numeric predicates; missing ties because PK dedup shrinks tables.
